text: @idavidrein DNA sequencing has improved by leaps and bounds but a lot of things happen going through transcription (DNA -> RNA) and translation (RNA -> Protein) including splicing the sequence and post translational modifications. By sequencing proteins we should be able to detect these.

author: TrentonBricken
text:
I argue this approach explicitly finds the set of “replaceable” tokens for a particular context and that languages (including that of biology) have this replaceability property.

If you’re interested please reach out and/or give me feedback.

author: TrentonBricken
text:
Tail Free Sampling tries to ensure you sample diverse and high quality sequences by finding where the probability distribution for the next token to be generated plateaus. 

Here is an example with different hyperparameters: 0.9 (green) and 0.95 (blue) tend to work well https://t.co/6NslQvQqlg

author: TrentonBricken
text:
Generating sequences from a language model using Ancestral, Top-K, or Nucleus Sampling? Consider using Tail Free Sampling instead! https://t.co/aRVkEgoBWU
